summary: Carlo Giussani was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore, University of Pisa, and University of Turin, with teachers including Bardelli, Weber, von Roth, Ascoli, and von Spiegel. He taught at Liceo Manin (~1866–1873) and Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano (1874–1900).
Carlo Jamelle Harris works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA in philosophy at National Chengchi University under the supervision of Chen-kuo Lin (attested 2009).

Carlo Puini was a scholar of Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Pisa. In 1877, he was appointed extraordinary professor of East Asian history and geography at the University of Florence.

Carlo Salvioni was a linguist who earned his PhD at the University of Leipzig under Karl Brugmann, after studying at Basel. He held posts at Turin, Pavia (1890–1902), and the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano from 1902.

Carlos Garcia-Jane specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Barcelona, Aberystwyth, South Wales, and Edinburgh (PhD 2022). He held posts at the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies, the Royal Central School of Speech and Drama, and Buddhist Studies Review.

Carmen Blacker was a scholar of Japanology and religious studies. She studied at SOAS, Somerville College, and Keio University under Shigeru Gorai. She served as a lecturer at the University of Cambridge from 1955 and chaired the Folklore Society (1982–1984).

Carmen Dragonetti was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy who studied at National University of San Marcos. She was a professor at the University of Buenos Aires (attested 1989) and vice director of the Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas (attested 2001).

Carmen Meinert is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology who completed her PhD at the University of Bonn in 2001. She held posts at the University of Hamburg (attested 2008) and Ruhr University Bochum (2013).
Carol A. Breckenridge worked in Indology and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968–1976) and later held a post at the University of Chicago.

Carol S. Anderson specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under W. S. Karunatillake and John A. Brinkman, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Kalamazoo College (attested 2004).

Carola Roloff is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned her doctorate at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson. She taught at the Tibetisches Zentrum Hamburg (2002–2010) and has held guest professorships and research posts at Hamburg and Oslo.
Carola S. Carstens works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She held a post at Rice University (1998–1999) and completed her doctorate at the University of Hamburg in 2006.
Carole M. Cusack is a religious studies scholar who completed her PhD at the University of Sydney (1988–1995), where she became Professor of Religious Studies in 2013.

Carole McGranahan is a Tibetologist and historian who studied at Colgate and completed her PhD at the University of Michigan under Nicholas Dirks and Ann Laura Stoler. In 2001, she joined the anthropology faculty at the University of Colorado Boulder.

Caroline Humphrey is an anthropologist of Iranian and Central Asian studies and religion. She studied at Cambridge and Leeds, working under Edmund Leach, and held academic posts at Cambridge from 1978 to 2010, along with a visiting professorship at Michigan in 2000.

Caroline Rhys Davids was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at UCL under George Croom Robertson and T. W. Rhys Davids, she served as Pali Text Society General Editor (1907–1942) and lectured at Manchester and SOAS.

Carolyn Woodford Schmidt is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar. She earned doctorates from Ohio State University under John C. Huntington and Wichita State University, and served as Director at the University of Kansas in 2017.
Carson T. Schütze is a linguist who studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from 1992 to 1997. He took up a post at the University of California, Los Angeles, in 1997.

Carsten Colpe was a scholar of religious and Iranian/Central Asian studies who studied under Hans Heinrich Schaeder (~1950–1954). He held posts at the University of Göttingen (~1956–1969) and the Free University of Berlin (~1969–1997).

Caterina Conio was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied at Florence, Cattolica del Sacro Cuore, and Banaras Hindu University under T. R. V. Murti and Paul Hacker. In 1974, she taught Indian religion and philosophy at Pisa.
